author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): fail the Pages build on Liquid errors, unmangle two live pages (#439)
body:
The Pages workflow was green while publishing damaged pages. `github-pages`
ships jekyll-optional-front-matter, so every non-excluded Markdown file in the
repo becomes a page and is run through Liquid before Markdown. Prose that
merely looks like a template is therefore executed as one — and Jekyll 3
reports that as a `Liquid Warning` on stdout, drops the expression, and still
exits 0. Nothing in CI read that output, so the corruption shipped.

Two pages were live on zer0-mistakes.com:

  /CHANGELOG/
    "Added ,, and to the template renderer" — three `{{VAR}}` placeholders,
    documenting the installer's own template tokens, evaluated to nothing.

  /_design-system/components/feedback/Skeleton.prompt/
    "<div style=>" — the JSX `style={{ … }}` in the specimen is a Liquid
    syntax error, so the attribute was dropped from the published example.

A third defect produced no warning at all: a literal raw tag written as prose
in a changelog entry opened a real Liquid block that swallowed the following
945 lines of the rendered page. That class cannot be gated on build output,
because Liquid does not consider a swallowed document an error.

Fixes:

  - Escape every unwrapped Liquid token in CHANGELOG.md (10 spans) and wrap
    the JSX fence in Skeleton.prompt.md. The design-system tree is a sync
    mirror, so SYNC.md now states the rule for the next pull rather than
    relying on it being rediscovered.
  - pages.yml tees both builds and fails on `Liquid Warning`/`Liquid
    …

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): make the pixel gate see the data files that move pixels (#425)
body:
Adds _data/navigation/**, ui-text.yml, i18n/**, theme_skins.yml and
theme_backgrounds.yml to ci.yml's `styling` paths-filter so chrome-affecting
data changes run Visual Snapshots instead of skipping it, plus a
lint-workflows.yml invariant that pins the coverage so the gap cannot silently
reopen. Also masks the minute-resolution theme-info build stamp in the
appearance snapshot spec.

Closes #417

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): fail the content review when it did not actually run (#424)
body:
An auth failure previously produced a green check on a review that never ran —
the CLI reported its 401 on stdout, so the non-empty output was posted as if it
were the review. Adds scripts/ci/agent_review_result.py, which classifies the
agent output and fails the step (with a ::error:: annotation) when the CLI
exited non-zero, produced nothing, or produced only a failure notice. Renames
the availability gate to reflect that a present credential is not a valid one.

Closes #418

author: Amr
subject: fix(layouts): move keyboard focus to the skip-link target (tabindex="-1") (#395)
body:
<main id="main-content"> is not natively focusable, so activating the skip link
scrolled the page while focus stayed on <body> and the next Tab returned the
user to the header nav they had just skipped (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). Adds
tabindex="-1" plus #main-content:focus { outline: none; } so the container does
not paint a ring while descendants keep theirs, with two Playwright regression
tests that activate the link and assert focus actually moved. Docs (en + fr)
updated to match the shipped markup.

Closes #278

author: dependabot[bot]
subject: chore(deps): bump github/codeql-action from 4.37.7 to 4.37.9 (#421)
body:
Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: github/codeql-action 4.37.7 to
4.37.9. Updates the default CodeQL bundle to 2.26.4.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): wait past the cold bundle install for Jekyll in the snapshot gate (#426)
body:
test/update-snapshots.sh hard-coded a 120s readiness ceiling for Jekyll on
:4000. On a cold runner the bundle_cache named volume is empty, so the container
runs a full bundle install and Jekyll's first site build before binding the
port — the poller gave up mid-build, which is why the Visual Snapshots job went
red only in CI. Makes the ceiling configurable via JEKYLL_READY_TIMEOUT and
defaults it to 420s. The loop still exits the moment curl succeeds, so warm
local runs are unaffected, and the failure path is unchanged.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ui-audit): serve without --detach so the sweep can capture, and fail loudly when it cannot (#434)
body:
jekyll serve --detach disables the watch thread the LiveReload reactor rides on,
so _config_dev.yml's livereload_port was bound but silent while Jekyll still
injected livereload.js into every page. The hanging subresource blocked `load`,
so every page.goto(..., waitUntil: 'load') timed out — the audit captured zero
evidence for six consecutive weeks and reported success each time, because
curl -sf never requests a subresource and sweep.mjs always exited 0.

Backgrounds the serve as test_playwright.sh does, tears it down in an always()
step, adds a capture floor to sweep.mjs and an independent assertion step, and
makes the sticky issue distinguish "N findings" from "captured nothing". Adds
test/ui-audit/check-audit-serve.sh as the red-before/green-after check.

Closes #321

author: Amr
subject: feat(includes): icon-only language trigger and a compact, positive menu (#431)
body:
Drops the EN text span and the dropdown-toggle caret from the navbar trigger
(38px square, title/aria-label now name the language being read, since they are
the only accessible name left). Replaces disabled rows with real links to the
source page carrying hreflang for the destination, marks the current language
with a tint plus bi-check2 instead of a primary .active fill, adds an "auto"
chip on machine translations, and collapses the per-row "(Not yet translated)"
text into one aria-describedby footnote. Menu capped at 220px with name
ellipsis: measured 243px before, 144px after.

Closes #406

author: Amr
subject: fix(layouts): upgrade the no-js class to "js" so the hook works (#428)
body:
_layouts/root.html shipped class="no-js" and nothing ever upgraded it, so the
progressive-enhancement hook was inert: every page on every downstream site
carried no-js with JavaScript fully enabled, and a consumer writing
html.js .foo {…} got the no-JS branch for everyone. Adds an inline,
un-deferred swap script as the first child of <head> — above core/head.html,
which opens with Google Tag Manager, so "first in that include" is not "first
in <head>" — since it must run before the first stylesheet or html.js rules
would flash.

The served HTML still carries class="no-js", so the JS-disabled branch stays
correct. Regression coverage in test/visual/core/progressive-enhancement.spec.js
pins both directions plus the delivery mechanism, because a fix that simply
deleted the attribute would satisfy a one-sided assertion while removing the
hook entirely.

Closes #319

author: github-actions[bot]
subject: chore(deps): update Ruby gem dependencies (#438)
body:
Gemfile.lock only: async 2.44.1 to 2.45.1, io-event 1.19.5 to 1.21.1, and
rubocop 1.89.0 to 1.90.0 (which relaxes its json constraint from ~> 2.3 to
>= 2.3). Quality Control, Test Suite and Integration Tests all pass on the
new lock.

author: Amr
subject: feat(includes): live preview, vertical stepper and draft persistence in the setup wizard (#432)
body:
Five changes to the dev-gated setup wizard, built in dependency order because
the height fix has to land before the stepper:

- Back/Next stop moving vertically: measurePanes() sets an inline min-height on
  the tab content equal to the tallest pane (CSS cannot know that height), plus
  margin-top: auto on .wizard-nav. Both rules are required.
- The YAML preview becomes a persistent sticky column, live from the first
  keystroke rather than refreshing on tab change only.
- Inline validation on blur for email and URL, with aria-describedby feedback.
  Empty is never an error — nothing in this wizard is required.
- Draft persistence to localStorage (debounced), restoring field values,
  checkbox states and the step you left off on, but only if that step still
  validates. A throwing localStorage is swallowed.
- nav-pills becomes a vertical .wizard-stepper with is-done/is-active/is-locked
  and a visually-hidden state string.

Closes #408

author: Amr
subject: fix(includes): footer Info/Cookie Preferences are buttons, not anchors (#427)
body:
The footer's two in-page dialog triggers open UI rather than navigating, so
they are <button type="button">, not <a href="#">. Both branches of the
powered-by loop are fixed, and the only remaining href="#" is the
#backToTopBtn anchor.

Rather than a `btn btn-link p-0` reset — which re-adds padding, line-height and
a 1px transparent border, shifting the box 2px — the class carries the reset:
.powered-by-link is now element-agnostic and .footer-inline-button is the same
reset for a button in running text. Also fixes two coverage regressions the
swap would otherwise have caused: the policy-row tap-target rule in
_footer.scss and the 24px check in responsive.spec.js both walked anchors only,
so the converted control would have silently left the WCAG 2.5.8 checks.

axe cannot detect this defect — an <a> with an href is well-formed to axe-core
and no rule fires on "anchor used as a button" — so the new test asserts
element identity directly.

Closes #320

author: github-actions[bot]
subject: chore(i18n): refresh machine-generated translations (#415)
body:
Regenerated fr/**, _data/i18n/*.yml and _data/i18n/manifest.yml from the
English source via scripts/translate.rb. Build artifacts only — never
hand-edited.

Visual Snapshots ran on this PR rather than being skipped, because #425 added
_data/i18n/** to ci.yml's styling filter.

author: Amr
subject: chore(main): release 1.29.0 (#383)
body:
Release 1.29.0. Bumps lib/jekyll-theme-zer0/version.rb, Gemfile.lock,
package.json, package-lock.json and .release-please-manifest.json in lockstep,
and regenerates _data/theme-manifest.yml as the release snapshot.

Generated by release-please.

author: Amr
subject: fix(includes): declare charset inside the 1024-byte window, make the feed discoverable (#440)
body:
The HTML spec only scans the first 1024 bytes for the character-encoding
declaration. <meta charset> sat in _includes/core/head.html below Google Tag
Manager, console-capture, page-views, mermaid and nanobar — and below two
multi-line HTML doc banners that ship verbatim — so a served page declared its
encoding at byte 26058. Past the limit a browser decodes with its locale
default, mangling every non-ASCII byte until it re-parses; the theme ships UTF-8
throughout, so this is a corruption risk rather than a lint nit.

Moving the tag was not the fix on its own: the top of core/head.html still left
it at 4415, and the top of root.html at 2204, because that file's own doc banner
is an HTML comment and ships. Converting it to a Liquid comment (stripped at
build) is what freed the budget. Measured at byte 318 across all 400 built
pages, exactly one declaration per head.

Also emits the jekyll-feed autodiscovery link the theme never called feed_meta
for, so /feed.xml existed but nothing advertised it. Written out directly rather
than via feed_meta so a consumer without the plugin does not hard-fail.

test/visual/core/head-contract.spec.js measures the SERVED BYTES — a source
order assertion would have passed before and after, and page.content() cannot
see it either since the parser hoists the charset. 3 of 4 fail on the parent
commit, all 4 pass here.

Closes #372
Closes #371

author: Claude
subject: test(evidence): before/after bundle for the dangling aria-controls fix
body:
The evidence gate was red: this PR touches _includes/, and a UI change needs a
regression test plus before/after evidence. The test was already there; this
adds the evidence.

`no-visual-change` would have been the easy way out and it would have been
FALSE. 37 pages genuinely lose a visible control — a 40x40 navbar toggle on the
admin-layout pages and a 56x56 TOC FAB on 404/CHANGELOG. Each did nothing when
clicked, but they were painted, so the honest route is evidence rather than the
opt-out label.

The change is Liquid, not CSS, so evidence-kit's unfixCss cannot show both
states from one server. aria-controls-evidence.mjs drives two servers instead —
one per build — and captures the same region from each.

Two corrections made while generating it, both recorded in the bundle README:

- The first 404 capture was at 1280px and produced two byte-identical empty
  crops, because .bd-toc-fab is d-lg-none: at desktop the dead control sat in
  the DOM painting nothing. Re-captured at 375px, where the visual half of the
  regression actually exists (4082 -> 1553 bytes).
- Added a measurement of each control's painted size, so the bundle can
  distinguish "removed from the DOM" from "removed from view".

The third case is a control: /docs/ renders both offcanvases and keeps all five
of its controls, byte-identical before and after. Without it, a fix that deleted
the controls everywhere would look equally good.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

where it has been cherry-picked as 5a41103. The repo's convention is a branch

author: Amr
subject: fix(a11y): give footer icon links an accessible name, announce search results (#441)
body:
Closes #435
Closes #279

#435 — the footer's "Follow Us" social links and the RSS link render an <i> that
is aria-hidden="true" beside a <span class="d-none d-md-inline"> label. Below the
md breakpoint the span is display:none, so it leaves the accessibility tree and
the link had NO accessible name at all: a screen reader announced a bare "link".
Measured on origin/main at 375px: 7 nameless links. Each now carries an
aria-label matching its visible text exactly, so the name is right on mobile and
still contains the visible label at md+ (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name).

#279 — the search modal rewrites its results container without moving focus, so
assistive tech got silence. Adds a visually-hidden role="status" aria-live
region carrying a concise count. The results list itself is deliberately NOT
live: announcing eight titles and snippets per keystroke would be unusable. A
repeated announcement is cleared before being re-set, or "No results found."
would stay silent as the user keeps typing characters that all miss.

test/visual/core/accessible-names.spec.js asserts at MOBILE width, which is the
whole point — the same assertions pass at desktop on the unfixed code, which is
how this survived the existing suite. Verified against real Jekyll builds: 3 of
4 fail on origin/main (7 nameless links; no status region) and all 4 pass here.
The Label-in-Name test passes both ways by design, guarding the new aria-label
against diverging from the visible text.


Claude-Session: https://claude…

author: Amr
subject: fix(a11y): stop emitting sidebar/TOC controls on layouts that render no offcanvas (#443)
body:
* fix(a11y): stop emitting sidebar/TOC controls on layouts that render no offcanvas

Closes #373

#bdSidebar (navigation/sidebar-left.html) and #tocContents
(navigation/sidebar-right.html) are emitted by _layouts/default.html alone, but
their toggles live in core/header.html and core/footer-fabs.html — both included
from _layouts/root.html, so they render on EVERY layout. On any layout that
inherits root directly (admin, stats, 404, section, home, book-*) the control
pointed at an offcanvas that was never in the document: inert on click, and
aria-controls dangling into nothing for assistive tech.

Measured on a 415-page build of origin/main: 19 pages with a dangling
#bdSidebar (the French /about/** tree, layout: admin) and 18 with a dangling
#tocContents (404, CHANGELOG, _design-system/**). Zero after.

sidebar-config.html now publishes `sidebar_offcanvas_rendered` and both controls
are gated on it. The unified mobile drawer is deliberately exempt:
#zer0UnifiedDrawer is emitted from root.html, so that target exists everywhere.

footer-fabs.html had a DENYLIST of layouts to skip, which fails open — any new
layout got the FAB whether or not it rendered the panel, and the list had
already fallen behind (404 and book-* were missing). Replaced with the positive
gate, which fails safe.

Liquid cannot resolve layout inheritance, so the allowlist is written out. It is
pinned by test_core.sh :: test_sidebar_offcanvas_layout_gate, which walks the
front matter of every _layouts/*.html, …

author: Amr
subject: chore(ci): close finished issues — backlog statuses and a nightly recovery path (#442)
body:
Closes #326

Two halves of the same defect: work that is done, whose issue stays open.

1. sync-backlog.rb treats _data/backlog.yml as the source of truth and REOPENS
   any issue whose task is not `done`. T-038, T-040 and T-045 shipped in v1.29.0
   (#431, #432, #425); their `Closes #NNN` commits closed #406, #408 and #417,
   and the next sync reopened all three because the backlog still said `open`.
   Marking them done — with their PR links — is the only thing that closes them.

2. nightly-extended.yml files and updates a sticky issue on failure and does
   nothing on recovery, so a fixed failure stays open forever. #326 sat open five
   days past its own fix, carrying a P1 into every triage pass. Adds a
   report-recovery job that comments and closes the sticky when the tier goes
   green.

   It is gated on preflight.outputs.go == 'true' as well as both jobs
   succeeding. A bare success() would be wrong: the preflight short-circuits on
   an unchanged main and both test jobs report `skipped`, which would close the
   issue on a night that tested nothing. Three of the six recent "green" nightly
   runs were exactly that.

_data/backlog.yml validates: scripts/sync-backlog.rb --check reports 44 tasks OK.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DJbb79zt4GiMuqoTNNh4TR

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: perf(includes): strip developer doc banners from delivered HTML (#445)
body:
* perf(includes): strip developer doc banners from delivered HTML

Closes #375.

Theme includes and layouts document themselves with multi-line
`<!-- ... -->` banners. HTML comments are payload: Jekyll copies them
verbatim into every rendered page, so file paths, dependency lists and
design rationale are shipped to every visitor on every request. Liquid
`{% comment %}` blocks are stripped at build time instead.

1,065 banners across 89 files. Only the delimiters change; the banner
text and its line structure are byte-identical, so `git diff -w` shows
just the two edges.

Measured across a 415-page build:

  delivered HTML   91,464,620 B -> 71,603,991 B   (21.7% removed)
  comment payload  19,877,745 B ->     46,277 B
  comment blocks        142,840 ->       1,405
  per page             47,898 B ->        111 B  (344 -> 3 blocks)

The per-page number dwarfs the 124,983-byte source diff because an
include's banner is re-emitted at every call site, not once:
/authors/default/ carried 130,840 bytes of it from post-card.html
rendering 1,100 times. A banner in a leaf component is paid per render.

Kept as HTML, deliberately: the four boundary markers inside Google's
own copy-paste analytics snippets, so those blocks stay diffable against
upstream. They are matched exactly, not by substring -- prose that
merely mentions GTM is a developer note like any other, and a substring
rule wrongly spared three of them. Comments inside <script>, <style>,
<pre>, <textarea> or a Liquid raw block…

author: Amr
subject: fix(content): raw-protect Liquid that is written as documentation (#446)
body:
* fix(content): raw-protect Liquid that is written as documentation

Liquid runs before Markdown, so backticks and code fences never escaped
it -- they only changed how its OUTPUT was displayed. Two published
pages executed the tags they meant to show.

CHANGELOG.md:311 wrote `{% include core/head.html %}` in prose. The
include ran, so the CHANGELOG page shipped a second full copy of <head>
inside its body:

  bootstrap.min.css     2 -> 1
  bootstrap-icons.css   2 -> 1
  X-UA-Compatible       2 -> 1
  assets/css/main.css   3 -> 2

On a production build that second copy also carries the Google Tag
Manager snippet, since head.html emits it under a jekyll.environment
gate that this sandbox build does not satisfy.

pages/_docs/customization/layouts.md put `{{ content }}` in a code fence
and again in the Layout Variables table. The table documented nothing:
`{{ content }}` injected the entire rendered page into a cell, breaking
out of the table, and `{{ page.title }}` rendered as the literal word
"Layouts". The page carried 196,608 bytes of leaked layout output where
a five-line sample belonged -- 426,687 B -> 230,079 B.

Both are wrapped in raw blocks, the idiom these same two files already
use correctly elsewhere (CHANGELOG.md:617, layouts.md:130 and :147).

Deliberately NOT touched: fr/docs/customization/layouts.md:87 carries
the same leak, but fr/** is generated by scripts/translate.rb from the
English source and is never hand-edited; it inherits this fix on the
next translati…

author: Amr
subject: fix(a11y): decouple heading size from heading level in theme chrome (#450)
body:
* fix(a11y): decouple heading size from heading level in theme chrome

Closes #436. WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).

Several components picked a heading element for its default FONT-SIZE
rather than its position in the document, then restyled it. Anyone
navigating an article by heading heard

  h1 -> h2 -> h6 -> h2 -> h5 -> h3 -> h6

Measured across a 415-page build, not estimated:

  pages with at least one level skip   391 -> 66
  total skips                        1,060 -> 173

The issue led with the cookie modal, correctly, but the aggregate says
the damage was concentrated in TWO pieces of site-wide chrome, each
hitting all 391 affected pages: the cookie modal (h2 title, h6
categories) and the settings offcanvas including the language panel (h2
title, h6 section labels). The language panel was not in the report and
was doing exactly the same thing on every page.

Size and level are now separate: <h3 class="h6"> keeps the small type
and states the real depth. Nothing moves visually.

author-card.html renders under an h2 in author-bio.html and under
different ancestors in eleven other call sites, so no hardcoded level is
right for all of them -- choosing h5 for its font-size is what produced
the h2 -> h5 skip. Its level is now include.heading_level, defaulting to
the historic 5 so every caller that does not pass it is unchanged;
author-bio passes 3.

THE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: the first pass changed the six h6 labels in
info-section.html and rebuilt. Total skips wen…

author: Amr
subject: feat(includes): add background-image.html for CSS-painted cover art (#451)
body: * feat(includes): add background-image.html for CSS-painted cover art Closes #401. The theme had a convention for cover art rendered as (preview-image.html always emits an escaped alt) and none for art painted as a CSS background. A background image is invisible to assistive technology, so a box painted with cover art and nothing else announces nothing at all. The correct pattern already existed by hand in three unconnected places -- components/abc-letter.html, the article rating stars, and components/theme-customizer.html -- without being a named convention. This gives it a home. Two branches, and the second is not optional: real image -> role="img" + escaped aria-label decorative -> aria-hidden="true", NO role, NO aria-label aria-hidden together with role="img" announces a graphic and then hides it, which is worse than either alone. DECORATIVE IS THE DEFAULT and the real-image branch has to earn it: a src AND a non-empty alt AND no explicit decorative flag. Written as a positive test because the failure mode of getting it backwards is role="img" aria-label="" -- an unnamed graphic -- and falling back to aria-hidden is the safe direction. That is not hypothetical. The first version tested `bgi_src == blank`, and every decorative call rendered as an unnamed graphic, because `x == blank` does NOT match nil in Liquid 4 -- blank matches empty strings and collections only. The render matrix caught it; reading the source would not have. Both the file and the te…

author: Amr
subject: fix(scripts): restore nested translation placeholders instead of leaking them (#452)
body:
translate.rb masks every non-translatable span in a line as a ⟦N⟧ token
before sending it to the model, then restores it. The patterns run coarse
first, so a span can be masked twice: Liquid inside a link destination
becomes `](⟦3⟧)` and is then masked again as a whole, and the same happens
to Liquid inside an inline code span.

unmask used a single gsub, and gsub never rescans its own replacement text.
One pass restored the outer span and stranded the inner token as a literal
⟦3⟧ on the page — 107 tokens across 23 generated pages, and where the masked
span was a URL it is a dead link (`[couleurs](⟦3⟧)` and `href="⟦24⟧"` in
fr/about/design.md, the whole Liquid variable table in
fr/docs/customization/layouts.md).

unmask now substitutes until the text stops changing, bounded by the pattern
count since nesting cannot run deeper than that, and refuses to return
anything still holding a placeholder. A corrupt page now fails its own job
(logged, counted, non-zero exit) instead of shipping.

The "no placeholder tokens leak" assertions in test_i18n.sh were correct but
toothless: no fixture line nested a mask. Both shapes are now in the fixture,
so the guard fails without the fix — 4 failures before, 99/0 after.

Already-generated pages are not repaired here: staleness is decided by source
SHA alone, so a masker fix does not make an unchanged page stale. Repairing
them needs a --full re-translation.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DJbb79zt4GiMuqoTNNh4TR

Co-authore…

author: Amr
subject: fix(install): stop seeding the theme's own navigation into consumers (#449)
body:
* fix(install): stop seeding the theme's own navigation into consumers

Closes #332.

install.sh copied the theme's entire _data/ into every consumer, so each
site's OWN _data/navigation/*.yml was a verbatim copy of the theme's and
carried the theme's page taxonomy. Measured on a real install into an
empty directory:

  106 of 129 seeded navigation URLs point at pages the installer does
  not create

docs.yml alone accounts for 45 of them -- the ~47-per-doc-page figure
htmlproofer reported on lifehacker.dev, ~1,598 across ~34 docs, none of
which a consumer could remove from their own content.

_data/navigation/ is now held back from the theme copy (install_theme_data
walks _data entry by entry) and seeded from
templates/data/navigation-*.yml.template instead. Every URL in those
templates resolves against a page the installer actually creates: 0 of 26
unresolvable after the fix.

THE RENDERER IS UNCHANGED, deliberately. `nav: tree` already resolves
through auto -> page.collection -> site.data.navigation[collection], and
_data is not part of Jekyll's theme payload, so site.data is always the
consumer's. The resolver was correct; it was handed the wrong data.

Two things the issue did not have:

1. The scope is all seven files, not docs.yml. main.yml seeds 6 dead
   links, about.yml 3, posts.yml 6, home.yml 1, admin.yml 1. The
   acceptance criteria asked for a decision on the siblings; the data
   makes it: every one of them is affected.

2. The template seeding at install.sh:8…

author: Amr
subject: feat(includes): make theme-color track the page surface, not the accent (#447)
body:
* feat(includes): make theme-color track the page surface, not the accent

Closes #281.

theme-color drives mobile browser chrome -- the iOS Safari address and
status bar, the Chrome/Android task-switcher card. Three defects:

1. Wrong source. It fell back to site.theme_color.main, the brand ACCENT
   (#007bff here), so a dark-first theme advertised a bright blue address
   bar. Chrome must track the SURFACE, --bs-body-bg.

2. No scheme awareness. One unconditional tag meant exactly one of a
   light-mode and a dark-mode visitor saw the seam this issue is about.

3. Consumers got nothing at all. The tag sat behind an {% if %} whose only
   fallback was a key remote_theme consumers do not have -- they do not
   inherit this repo's _config.yml (remote-theme-checklist.md). Nil in,
   nothing out, on exactly the sites the include exists to serve. That is
   the observation the issue was filed on.

Defaults are Bootstrap 5.3.3's own --bs-body-bg per scheme (:root #fff,
[data-bs-theme=dark] #212529); the theme adds no dark override of that
variable, so those are the real computed surfaces. New optional
favicon.theme_color_light / theme_color_dark override them.

WHICH SHAPE IS EMITTED depends on how the mode is decided, because
media="(prefers-color-scheme: ...)" keys off the OS and nothing else:

  empty config / color_mode_default: auto  -> both tags, one per scheme
  color_mode_default: dark | light         -> one unconditional tag
  color_mode_lock: true                    -> o…

author: Amr
subject: fix(sass): stop navbar controls flickering under a stationary pointer (#453)
body:
.nav-link:hover, the Search/Settings utility buttons and the two
sidebar/TOC FABs applied transform: translateY(-1px). A lift moves the
element out from under a pointer parked on the row it vacates, so hover
exits, the element drops back under the pointer, and hover re-enters —
an infinite flicker with no pointer movement at all.

Deleting those declarations was not sufficient. _ui-enhancements.scss
applies transform: translateY(-2px) to .btn:hover — every button in the
theme. These controls are .btns, so with the navbar's own lift removed
they kept flickering on the inherited one: measured on the built site,
the Settings button lost and regained hover 14 times in 800ms with the
pointer completely still. The fix cancels it explicitly with
`transform: none`, the corrective pattern already used in
_post-navigation.scss and the prefers-reduced-motion blocks. The pressed
cue moves to :active, which is safe because it only holds while the
button is held down.

Three corrections to the issue as filed:

- The vacated row is the BOTTOM edge, not the top. A probe parked on the
  top edge passes without exercising the bug at all.
- Only a transform on the hovered element's own box can flicker.
  `&:hover i { transform: scale(1.1) }` moves a child and never shrinks
  the parent's hit box; those went for consistency, not as causes.
- `.nav-link:hover`, named as the primary culprit, was dead code. Its
  lift sits inside @media (min-width: 992px) { @container navbar-main
  (max-width: 75re…

Why: the agents that author UI PRs mostly run where Docker is gated or
absent, so PR #454 arrived with a README-only evidence folder (which the
gate accepted) and nine legitimately stale baselines that CI could report
but nothing could refresh.

subject: fix(ci): run the autogen lane's tooling from the base branch, not the PR (#464)
body:
The lane's first real run on a real PR died 20 seconds in:

  python3: can't open file 'scripts/ci/visual_evidence_autogen.py'

visual-evidence-autogen.yml checks out the PR's head branch, but the
orchestrator lives on main. #454 was cut before the lane shipped, so its
branch has no copy — and that is not an edge case, it is every open PR on
the day the lane lands. It failed on the very PR it was built to unstick.

A branch carrying an OLDER copy would have been worse than one carrying
none: #454's test/update-snapshots.sh predates the PRE_TEST_SCRIPT /
POST_TEST_SCRIPT / SKIP_PLAYWRIGHT hooks, so generation would have
silently no-opped and the run would have reported success having produced
nothing.

The workspace stays the PR's branch; the lane's own tooling (LANE_TOOLING
— the orchestrator, both shared generators, update-snapshots.sh) is now
restored from the base ref first, then immediately unstaged so it can
never ride along in the artifact commit. The PR's own
test/visual/<slug>-evidence.mjs is deliberately NOT overwritten: shipping
one is the point. This also closes a hole where a PR could rewrite the
orchestrator that CI then executes with `contents: write`.

Verified against the real branch: restoring into a worktree of
agent/issue-405 turns "No such file" into a working planner —
`needed=True jobs=1 snapshots_in_scope=True ui_files=5`, correctly routed
to that PR's own bespoke navbar-tiers generator — with nothing staged.

author: Amr
subject: fix(includes): expose skin-button selected state via aria-pressed (#469)
body:
The Theme Skin toggle group in Settings -> Appearance conveyed selection
only through the Bootstrap `.active` class, which carries no
accessibility semantics. Screen readers announced nine identical
unlabelled buttons with no indication of which skin was applied --
WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). The sibling color-mode group in
the same panel already does this correctly, so the two toggle groups in
one panel behaved inconsistently.

Each button now renders `aria-pressed`, true on the configured skin and
false on the rest. Both mutation sites -- the click handler and the
"Reset background" re-highlight -- route through one
`markActiveSkinButton` helper so no code path can leave `.active` and
`aria-pressed` disagreeing.

Regression test added to test/visual/features/settings-panel.spec.js,
modelled on the existing color-mode assertions. It asserts the attribute
directly rather than via axe: no wcag2a/wcag2aa rule fires on a toggle
button missing aria-pressed, so an axe check would pass on the broken
and fixed markup alike.

Closes #467

Co-authored-by: claude[bot] <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): stop the UI audit reporting a measurement blackout as a clean run (#471)
body:
* fix(ci): stop the UI audit reporting a measurement blackout as a clean run

sweep.mjs built each page with browser.newPage(), which
@axe-core/playwright refuses ("Please use browser.newContext()"). The
throw landed in a single per-route `try` that also discarded the
overflow, console-error and link-collection data ALREADY gathered for
that route -- so one library misuse erased four working measurements on
every route. Screenshots ran before the throw and kept succeeding, so
the harness looked alive: 18 of 21 passes captured, the #321 wipeout
guard stayed quiet, and the report rendered the absence as "0 axe
violations / 0 broken links". That reads as a mostly-healthy audit
rather than a dead one.

- Pages come from browser.newContext() -> context.newPage(), closed per
  iteration. reducedMotion is set on the context so it applies during
  load, and the fullPage screenshot gets a timeout that covers pages
  tens of thousands of pixels tall -- together these fix the /features/
  timeout that cost the other 3 passes.
- Every measurement is independent, recording its own error on
  entry.errors.<name>. A broken measurement now costs exactly itself.
- Absent is not zero: a scan that threw is reported as UNKNOWN, never as
  clean, and report.json carries links_checked so "broken: 0" has a
  denominator.
- A measurement that failed on EVERY route is a harness fault and exits
  1 -- the #321 capture floor, applied per measurement, which is the
  gap this bug fell through.
- The work…

author: Amr
subject: fix(navigation): stop Liquid whitespace-trim gluing navbar attributes (#477)
body:
* fix(a11y): stop Liquid trim markers gluing navbar attributes together

The conditional aria-current in _includes/navigation/navbar.html was wrapped
in whitespace-trimming Liquid markers at four sites (52, 82, 99, 128). The
leading {%- ate the newline after the preceding attribute and the trailing -%}
the whitespace before the following one, so the primary nav rendered
aria-label="News"aria-current="page"title="News" — the WHATWG
missing-whitespace-between-attributes parse error.

Two of the four sites sit between two unconditional attributes, so both markers
fire whether or not the conditional emits anything: those emitted invalid
markup on EVERY page for every nav item, not only the current one. Parsers
recover, which is why this went unnoticed across ~9 remote_theme consumers, but
the attributes involved are exactly aria-label, aria-current and title, and a
strict parser may drop the "you are here" announcement.

All four now use the non-trimming {% if %} form already present at line 26 of
the same file, with the separator outside the tag. Output is byte-different and
visually identical.

Guarded by test_navbar_attribute_whitespace in test/test_core.sh, which renders
the real include through Liquid — not a line-number slice — across both
aria-current branches and both nav modes, following the existing
background-image/theme-color contract-check idiom in that file.

Closes #465

author: Amr
subject: fix(layouts): one main landmark per page on post, notebook and note (#487)
body:
* fix(layouts): one main landmark per page on post, notebook and note

`_layouts/{article,notebook,note}.html` each rendered
`<article id="main" role="main">` inside root.html's `<main id="main-content">`,
so every post, notebook and note page exposed two `main` landmarks. ARIA
requires that landmark to be unique: duplicated, "skip to main content" and
landmark-rotor navigation are ambiguous in NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver (WCAG 2.1
SC 1.3.1). The role also overrode the element's native `article` landmark, so
the post stopped being announced as an article at all.

Same class of defect as #299, which removed a nested literal `<main>`; the
`role` attribute re-created the identical condition on a different element.
`_layouts/default.html:93-94` already carries the comment that fix left behind.

The generic `id="main"` goes with it. Nothing in the theme references `#main` —
the skip link targets `#main-content` — so it was an id squatting on a name
with no referents.

Microdata is untouched, and the rendered pixels are identical: no selector in
`_sass/` or `assets/js/` matches `#main` or `[role="main"]`.

test/visual/core/landmarks.spec.js pins it in two layers: a source assertion
over `_layouts/*.html` (no server, so it also covers `notebook`, whose
collection is `output: false` in `_config_dev.yml`) and rendered assertions per
route, including axe's `landmark-no-duplicate-main` — a best-practice rule the
existing `wcag2a`/`wcag2aa` audits never ran, which is why they stayed green
throug…

author: Amr
subject: feat(theme): four consumer extension points for notes/knowledge-base builds (#492)
body:
* feat(theme): four consumer extension points for notes/knowledge-base builds

Four gaps found while building it-journey's notes workbench (it-journey#634),
each a contained fix that helps any consumer building notes, docs, or a
knowledge base on this theme. The theme is consumed UNPINNED via remote_theme,
so a downstream workaround for a missing extension point is not a small risk —
it is one that fires on our schedule, silently, on a site we do not test.

1. Scope the code-copy button rule (the one with real blast radius).
   `_sass/core/code-copy.scss` shipped `.button, button:not(.copy)` with no
   scope at all — an element selector in a component partial, so it restyled
   EVERY button on a consumer site: `padding: 0 20px`, `font-size: 11px`, and a
   hardcoded `#bbb` that bypassed the tokens. At specificity (0,1,1) it also
   out-ranked `.btn` and any consumer's own class, so escaping it meant a
   specificity fight rather than a cascade. Now scoped to `.code-block-header` /
   `pre.highlight` and written in `--zer0-*` tokens; `#bbb` is gone from the
   compiled stylesheet.

2. Publish a code-block lifecycle event. `assets/js/code-copy.js` dispatches a
   bubbling `zer0:code-block-ready` per block with
   `{ wrapper, header, pre, code, lang }`, and exposes `zer0OnCodeBlock(fn)` —
   which REPLAYS `window.__zer0CodeBlocks` before subscribing. The replay is
   the load-bearing half: the sweep runs on DOMContentLoaded, so a deferred
   consumer script is normally later and…

subject: build(docker): harmonize Docker configuration to the fleet standard (#494)
